1: # ML-Based Stock Price Direction Prediction with Explainable AI
2: 
3: A master's-thesis project that builds a complete, leakage-free pipeline for
4: next-day stock-movement prediction, explains the resulting models with SHAP,
5: paraphrases the explanations with an LLM, evaluates the signals for trading
6: actionability, and packages everything into a browsable Flask demo.
7: 
8: The three classifiers (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost), trained
9: on 23 technical indicators for 28 stocks over 2018-2026, all perform at the
10: chance level under a strictly leakage-free walk-forward protocol
11: (roughly 50% balanced accuracy, ROC AUC ~ 0.50, MCC ~ 0). A cross-sectional
12: extension that adds daily relative rank and z-score features and scores the
13: daily Rank-IC reproduces the same null result. The project is therefore a
14: careful demonstration of how to test and falsify a momentum-style technical
15: signal: it traces an apparent 20-day "signal" to a walk-forward leak, corrects
16: it, and shows that no out-of-sample edge survives. This is consistent with the
17: weak form of the Efficient Market Hypothesis.
18: 
19: **Explanatory research demo only. Nothing in this repository is trading
20: advice.**
21: 
22: ## Repository layout
23: 
24: ```
25: app.py                 Flask web UI (stock / model / day -> explanation)
26: src/                   All pipeline and analysis scripts
27: Data/                  Raw + cleaned CSV data (gitignored, not committed)
28: Results/               Metrics, SHAP arrays, caches, LLM log (gitignored)
29: Plots/                 Generated figures (gitignored)
30: static/                UI stylesheet + precomputed waterfall PNGs
31: templates/             Legacy Jinja templates (the served UI is generated in app.py)

33: ```

62: ## Leakage-free protocol (why the numbers are trustworthy)
63: 
64: The headline results use walk-forward cross-validation with expanding
65: training windows: 20-day test windows, a minimum 60% training share, three
66: seeds averaged on probabilities, a per-window `StandardScaler` fit only on
67: the training segment (and only for Logistic Regression), and an explicit
68: one-day buffer between the last training row and the first test label. An
69: early version of the pipeline showed an apparent edge at the 20-day horizon;
70: this was traced to the training window including rows whose labels overlapped
71: the test period (boundary look-ahead). After correcting the protocol every
72: model returned to the noise floor.
73: 
74: ## Web interface
75: 
76: ```
77: python app.py      # then open http://127.0.0.1:5000
78: ```
79: 
80: Pick a stock (10 pilot stocks), a model, and a day, and the page shows the
81: prediction with its UP probability and chance baseline, the actual outcome,
82: the top-5 SHAP contributions, a horizontal SHAP contribution bar chart
83: (positive contributions green, negative red, value labelled at each bar tip),
84: and a natural-language explanation. Explanations are drawn from the cached
85: 50-case verification log where available, otherwise generated live via the
86: Gemini API (key from `GEMINI_API_KEY` env var or `~/.gemini_api_key`; model
87: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` by default, override with `GEMINI_MODEL`). Cases can
88: be deep-linked with query parameters, e.g.
89: `http://127.0.0.1:5000/?stock=AAPL&model=XGBoost&date=2025-08-06`.
90:

93: Python 3.x (developed on 3.11). There is no `requirements.txt`; install the

98: ```

102: expects the precomputed cache under `Results/ui_cache/` (built by
103: `src/UI_precompute.py`).

105: ## Key results
106: 
107: Pooled over 28 stocks, 22,520 leakage-free out-of-sample predictions:
108: 
109: | Model | Accuracy | Balanced acc. | Base rate | ROC AUC | MCC |
110: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
111: | Logistic Regression | 50.3% | 49.6% | 53.2% | 0.498 | -0.008 |
112: | Random Forest | 50.2% | 50.1% | 53.2% | 0.503 | 0.001 |
113: | XGBoost | 50.1% | 50.0% | 53.2% | 0.502 | -0.000 |
114: 
115: Pooled McNemar p = 1.00 (no pairwise difference). Cross-sectional extension
116: (69 features, 22,460 predictions): best daily mean Rank-IC 0.0065, i.e. within
117: the band of pure chance and far below the ~0.02 threshold at which published
118: factor libraries consider daily IC tradeable.
119:

123: - src/Learning_curves.py — train/validation log-loss curves vs training size (per stock/model)
124: - src/train_test_loss_all.py — generates train/test log-loss learning curves for all 28 stocks (3 models) and saves Results/train_test_loss/train_test_loss_all.csv and Plots/train_test_loss_all/tl_{TICKER}.png

- Multi-day forward return (3/5d), sign of excess return vs SPY (alpha), filter |ret|>threshold to reduce noise
- Class balance changes; evaluate on actionable subset

3) Modeling (time-series nested CV for selection)
- Class weights (LR/RF) and scale_pos_weight (XGB) under strict WF
- LR L1/L2 C sweep, RF depth/leafs, XGB gamma/min_child_weight/reg_lambda
- Ensembles: stacking on WF out-of-fold, probability averaging
- Calibration (Platt/Isotonic) where thresholding matters

4) Data/robustness
- Liquidity filters, survivorship awareness, transaction costs/slippage in evaluation
- Regime-aware (separate models per regime) or regime features

5) Evaluation focus
- Precision@k, Sharpe-like, MCC, Brier, calibration, profitability after costs (not just accuracy)

- Add SPY/market-relative returns (integrate Enhance_features + index)
- XGB: gamma 0-1, min_child_weight 1-5, colsample_bytree 0.6-0.8
- RF: max_depth 6-9, min_samples_leaf 10-20
